title: Install runway: weekly scrub + customer escape-hatch
content:
Weekly install runway scrub - notes, rough tech debt, and a proposed escape-hatch for stretched installs. Informal — capture of the 05/14 weekly sync (30m).

Attendees: Maya (lead), Ben (field), Isha (network), Luca (observability), Samira (support oncall)
Meeting goal: surface installs at risk this sprint, agree temporary mitigations (escape-hatch), and assign owners for follow-up.

Quick status roll (by customer):
- Cust-A (large fintech, VPC): failing at BGP peer stage intermittently. Symptoms: route flaps after kube-proxy restart; agent loses control-plane auth for ~45s. Logs: agent heartbeat shows TLS handshake timeout 1.2. Recent change: bumped env proxy policy (PLAT-4523).
  - Current impact: degraded warmstart time, cron jobs backlogged.
  - Immediate mitigation proposed: enable fallback route via nat-gw (escape-hatch) for control-plane traffic while we debug BGP timers. Owner: Isha (run NAT change with field ops). Due: 2025-05-16
  - Follow-ups: gather tcpdump on control-plane (Ben), capture kernel logs around flaps (Samira).

- Cust-B (on-prem, high-latency datacenter): install stalled at container image pull (registry auth failures intermittently). Pattern: works with curl but containerd fails due to 401 retries then eventual 403. Probable cause: clock skew on installer host (ran into similar once).
  - Impact: install not completing, rollout blocked.
  - Short-term escape-hatch: pre-pull images to local mirror and skip remote pull stage (installer flag: --skip-remote-pull). Owner: Ben. Due: 05/15 EOD.
  - Longer: add clock sync check to preflight script (PR linked). Owner: Maya + Installer team.

- Cust-C (edge/onprem hybrid): KV-cache eviction causing inference flakiness post-upgrade. Observed: tail latency spikes after upgrade when traffic resumes; kv cache misses 3–5x baseline for first 10 minutes.
  - Mitigation: enable staged rollout with traffic-shaping and keep warm instances alive for 15m post-upgrade. Action: add rollout pre-sleep to deploy pipeline (PR referenced). Owner: Luca. Due: 05/19.

Cross-cutting blockers and notes:
- Observability gaps: we still can't correlate agent TLS restarts to upstream route events quickly. Need a small instrumentation spike: add a single trace/span emitted when agent re-establishes control-plane session (low overhead). Proposed owner: Luca (obs) + Isha (agent). Impacts schedule if not done (we keep losing time debugging).
- Installer telemetry: preflight returns boolean OK/FAIL only; we need structured failure codes for common failure classes (network, auth, disk). Ticket PLAT-4590 created. Owner: Installer lead.
- Oncall-to-install handover: recent field case showed support did not have direct shell access to jumpbox for customer -- created internal checklist entry: "verify remote-admin SSH key + jumpbox playbook". Owner: Samira.

Escape-hatch patterns (working draft):
1) Control-plane NAT fallback: when BGP or upstream routes are unstable, flip control-plane egress to customer-configured NAT gateway for a bounded window (5–30m), then revert. Pros: keeps installs progressing; Cons: requires network change approval. Implementation: small ansible play run by field ops via runbook.
2) Local image mirror + --skip-remote-pull: for flaky registries. Pros: quick; Cons: requires space on host and mirror maintenance. Add to preflight as optional quick path.
3) Warm-preserve flag for rollout: keep a minimum set of old instances alive for X minutes to smooth KV cache warm-up. Pros: stabilizes latency spikes; Cons: higher transient cost.

Action items (short):
- Isha: run NAT fallback for Cust-A on 05/16, paste runbook snippet and approval steps in this doc.
- Ben: produce tcpdump + containerd debug logs for Cust-A and Cust-B respectively, attach to PLAT-4523. Due 05/16.
- Luca: prototype agent re-connect trace and add to nightly build (small flag). Due 05/21.
- Maya: open PR to add clock-sync check into installer preflight and drive review. Due 05/18.
- Samira: update handover checklist and confirm jumpbox keys for active installs. Due 05/17.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How do we get network owners to approve temporary NAT changes quickly? Idea: pre-authorized IP ranges signed in contract appendices (legal). Need guidance from GTM/AE.
- Can we make image mirror creation non-interactive for field ops? Ops burden is the blocker.

Notes from the field (Ben):
- Seen two installs where vendor load balancer silently rewrote host headers; forced us to enable host-preserve mode in kube-proxy. Add host-preserve to preflight detection heuristics.
- Found small race in installer when /var/lib/redwood is created by post-install script before the agent writes its socket — leads to 2s failure that cascades to healthcheck flapping. Will propose a 1-line fix.

Telemetry snippets to collect (Luca):
- agent_reconnect_count{reason}
- control_plane_e2e_ms (last 5 minutes)
- kv_cache_miss_rate (per deploy window)

Meeting retrospective (fast):
- What's working: quick ad-hoc escape-hatch pattern is helping unblock installs. Field + install team coordination improved this sprint.
- What's not: small observability gaps and installer preflight shallow errors are costing several hours across customers.

Notes-to-self / scribbles:
- Draft runbook step for NAT fallback (very high level):
  1. Confirm CIDR and BGP peer keys with customer (support SLA doc)
  2. Provision temporary NAT in customer subnet or ask for routing rule change
  3. Update agent egress to NAT IP via ansible change and restart agent
  4. Monitor TLS handshakes + control-plane heartbeat for 10 minutes
  5. Revert when stable and capture tcpdump+metrics windows

- Keep this doc as living runbook until we fold into confluence checklist.

Last checked: created quick PRs for preflight checks and installer doc links placed in linked_artifacts above. Will iterate on runbook after NAT playbook test on 05/16.

-- Maya
